title: SRK and Sachin-Backed Purple Style Labs Eyes ₹660 Crore IPO Launch
excerpt: The parent company of luxury fashion platform Pernia's Pop-Up Shop, backed by Shah Rukh Khan, Sachin Tendulkar, Madhuri Dixit, and other celebrity investors, is preparing to go public after receiving SEBI approval in January.
body:
• Purple Style Labs, parent of Pernia's Pop-Up Shop, plans to raise ₹660 crore through an entirely fresh issue of equity shares with no offer-for-sale component.
  • Celebrity investors include Shah Rukh Khan, Salman Khan, Sachin Tendulkar, Madhuri Dixit, and Mahesh Babu, alongside institutional backers such as Volrado (Enam Holdings) and Singularity AMC.
  • The company operates over 15 experience centres worldwide and serves customers in more than 100 countries, with stores planned for New York, San Francisco, and Dubai.
  • Proceeds will fund expansion of retail experience centres (₹363 crore), sales and marketing (₹128 crore), and general corporate purposes.

The IPO Structure

Purple Style Labs Ltd, the Mumbai-based parent company of luxury fashion platform Pernia's Pop-Up Shop, is moving toward an initial public offering that could raise ₹660 crore. The company filed its draft red herring prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Board of India in September 2025 and received regulatory approval in January 2026.

The proposed IPO is structured as an entirely fresh issue of equity shares with a face value of ₹10 each, with no offer-for-sale component from existing shareholders. The company had also explored a pre-IPO placement of up to ₹130 crore, which would reduce the fresh issue size if completed.

Axis Capital and IIFL Capital Services have been appointed as book-running lead managers, with KFin Technologies as the registrar.

A Star-Studded Cap Table

What sets this IPO apart from other luxury fashion listings is its celebrity-heavy investor roster. Shah Rukh Khan, Salman Khan, Sachin Tendulkar, Madhuri Dixit, and Telugu star Mahesh Babu all hold stakes in the company, giving it unusual brand visibility in a market where luxury fashion platforms are still establishing consumer trust.

"The company has delivered about 100 times returns from the seed capital stage, even before the IPO price or valuation discovery."

— Purple Style Labs filing

Institutional investors form the backbone of the cap table. Volrado (Enam Holdings) is the largest institutional shareholder, followed by Akash Bhansali and Singularity AMC, the fund managed by veteran investor Madhu Kela. SageOne, Alchemy, and Value Quest are also invested, alongside family offices of Binny Bansal, Pidilite, Utpal Sheth, and others.

The company raised approximately 0 million in a Series E round in March 2025, led by SageOne Flagship Growth OE Fund, Alchemy Long Term Ventures, Bajaj Holdings, and Minerva Ventures.

The Business Behind the Brand

Founded in 2015 by Abhishek Agarwal, Purple Style Labs acquired Pernia's Pop-Up Shop in 2018 and has since scaled it into one of India's largest multi-brand luxury omnichannel fashion platforms. The company curates roughly 2.12 lakh SKUs across womenswear, menswear, fine jewellery, fashion jewellery, kidswear, and accessories from over 1,312 active designer brands including Tarun Tahiliani, Falguni Shane Peacock, and Gaurav Gupta.

Revenue has grown at a compound annual rate exceeding 100 per cent between FY21 and FY24, crossing ₹500 crore in consolidated revenue in FY24. The average order value climbed from ₹39,499 in FY23 to ₹56,106 in FY25, while sales and marketing expenses as a share of revenue dropped from 12.88 per cent to 6.77 per cent over the same period — a sign of improving unit economics.

Where the Money Will Go

The bulk of IPO proceeds — ₹363.3 crore — is earmarked for investment in its wholly owned subsidiary PSL Retail, specifically for lease liabilities related to experience centres and back-end offices across India. Another ₹128 crore will fund sales and marketing, including digital campaigns, social media advertising, influencer collaborations, and end-of-season promotions. The remainder goes toward general corporate purposes.

The company currently operates over 15 Pernia's Pop-Up Studio experience centres in cities including Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Ahmedabad, and Surat, plus one in Mayfair, London. Planned expansions target New York, San Francisco, Los Angeles, Dubai, and Singapore, along with domestic tier-II cities like Chandigarh, Indore, and Lucknow.

What It Means for Diaspora Shoppers

For NRIs who have traditionally relied on trips home or informal networks for Indian designer fashion, Pernia's Pop-Up Shop has emerged as one of the few platforms offering curated access to premium Indian designers with international shipping. The company served customers from more than 100 countries in FY25 through its online channels and its London flagship.

A successful IPO and the planned global expansion could further formalize that access, particularly in US and Middle East markets where demand for Indian occasion wear — bridal, festive, formal — remains strong.
nri_angle: Pernia's Pop-Up Shop serves Indian designer fashion buyers in 100+ countries and is expanding to New York, San Francisco, and Dubai — directly relevant to NRI shoppers seeking premium Indian occasion wear.
